title: Technical Guidance: One-Time Password (OTP) Theft and Account Takeover Vectors
content:
Credential theft and One-Time Password (OTP) extraction represent primary mechanisms for unauthorized account takeover and fraudulent fund dissipation.

1. OTP Harvesting Mechanisms:
Fraudsters employ multiple vectors to intercept authentication tokens:
- Fake Verification Webforms: Replicas of banking login portals that prompt the user for username, password, and secondary OTP token in real time (man-in-the-middle phishing).
- Vishing (Voice Phishing): Attackers pose as fraud department agents claiming an unauthorized transaction is underway and instructing the victim to recite the OTP 'to cancel the debit'. In reality, the attacker initiates a transfer and uses the dictated OTP to authorize it.
- Remote Access Tools: Persuading victims to install screen-sharing software (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk) under the guise of technical troubleshooting, enabling attackers to view incoming SMS OTP notifications directly on screen.

2. Key Safety Invariants:
- OTPs are single-use cryptographic authorization codes. Sharing an OTP is functionally equivalent to authorizing a transaction.
- Legitimate service providers and banks never request OTPs to cancel transactions, refund money, or verify account identity.
- If an OTP message states 'Do not share this code', this warning applies unconditionally to all callers, including individuals claiming to represent the issuing institution.
